title: Ryan OS Asset
description: One operational resource in the Ryan OS Asset Registry. Every asset must answer five questions: what is it, where is it, who owns it, when should it be used, and what does it replace.

asset_id.description: Stable slug. Referenced by playbooks and other assets - do not change it once published.

name.description: Human name as people actually refer to it.

status.description: authoritative = the one true version, use it. candidate = exists but not yet blessed. deprecated = superseded, do not use. gap = Ryan OS knows this resource should exist but has no authoritative version on file.

what_it_is.description: One or two sentences. What the thing actually is.

where_it_is.description: Where to find it. A gap asset may have kind 'unknown'.

path.description: Repo-relative path, URL, Drive path, UNC path, or launch command.

detail.description: How to actually get to it - which route, which menu, which share.

owner.description: Person or role accountable for keeping it correct.

use_when.description: The trigger. When should an agent or a person reach for this?

do_not_use_when.description: Boundaries. Prevents an asset being stretched past what it is good for.

replaces.description: Asset ids or free-text names this supersedes. This is how old versions stop circulating.

replaced_by.description: Required when status is deprecated. The asset_id that took over.

keywords.description: Search terms an agent might use. Add the wrong-but-common names too - that is how lookups succeed.

gap_recommendation.description: Required when status is gap. What Ryan should add, and why it matters.

last_verified.description: YYYY-MM-DD. When someone last confirmed this is still true.
